minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved the Q3 FY2025 commitment and the FY26 budget for presentation to the Finance Committee.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission accepted the third quarter commitment, three sets of minutes, and the final FY26 budget for its Finance Committee presentation on Thursday. Staff reported on the assistant business manager hire, MUNIS problems printing demand notices, and a legal question over a demand fee. The commission also discussed ways to recruit more commissioners.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; staff reported no public present.

votes.motion: Accept the third quarter FY2025 commitment letter.
Accept the minutes of three prior meetings (dates heard as 12/1/25, 12/8/25 and 2/11/25).
Accept the final version of the FY26 budget for presentation to the Finance Committee.

budget_items.what_was_said: Billing was run and printed, and the commitment numbers were reviewed and signed by commissioners before the vote.
A formula mistake in a spreadsheet raised the total retained earnings appropriation above what commissioners had earlier voted. The change was described as small.
A share of customer bills is unpaid, which in next year's budget works out to a sizeable amount. Staff said that if customers paid, retained earnings would not need to be drawn.
The district holds about $2 million in retained earnings, so using some to balance the budget was not seen as harmful.
Debt service to the neighboring city runs roughly ten more years. Estimated betterment revenues now slightly exceed the town debt service.

budget_items.topic: Lost demand fees from MUNIS printing failure
budget_items.what_was_said: Since the MUNIS upgrade, demand notices could not be printed, which staff said equates to substantial losses. A demand fee appeared in MUNIS but was never sent out, raising a question of whether it can be legally charged.

decisions.decision: The town director will present the FY26 budget to the Finance Committee on Thursday at 7 PM; commissioners are welcome to attend.
Bill will check with the town manager and social media staff about parameters; Scott will draft a volunteer recruitment post for local social media groups, framed as a citizen.
Next agenda to include budget information, the manhole repair IFB, an update on the assistant to the business manager position, and commissioner recruitment.
Upcoming meetings set: March 11 (hybrid, DPW building), March 25 (Zoom), April 8 (hybrid), April 29 (Zoom).

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the final FY26 budget for presentation to the Finance Committee.
The commission voted to accept the third quarter FY2025 commitment letter after commissioners reviewed and signed the commitment numbers.
Staff said demand notices could not be printed after the MUNIS upgrade, and a legal question is open on whether an unsent demand fee can be charged.
The town director is to present the FY26 budget to the Finance Committee on Thursday at 7 PM; commissioners may attend.
Commissioners discussed recruiting more commissioners; one is to draft a social media post, and another is to check parameters with the town.

why_it_matters: The FY26 sewer budget draws on retained earnings, and staff said unpaid customer bills drive that draw, so collection affects how much reserve is used.
Demand notices that could not be printed since the MUNIS upgrade mean late-payment collection was disrupted, and the legal opinion on the demand fee is still pending.
The sewer budget now goes to the Finance Committee, the next public step before it reaches a town vote.
